21st_magic_component_builder.rationale: The tool returns UI code: `ONLY returns the text snippet for that UI component`, and the schema says it searches `21st.dev (library for searching UI components)`. Public/component-library content may be outside-authored and attacker-controllable under the public registry/content threat model. The advertisement does not state whether 21st.dev results are curated or user-generated, so this is undetermined and the UNTRUSTED label is kept. It does not advertise editing files itself (`After calling this tool, you must edit or add files`), arbitrary host execution, or delivery to an attacker-chosen destination.

logo_search.rationale: The tool performs external logo search and returns code/markup: `Search and return logos`, `Returns TypeScript React component`, `Returns JavaScript React component`, and `Returns raw SVG markup`. Logo/search result data is public outside content and may be outside-authored. The text does not settle whether the logo source is curated or can include attacker-controlled public entries, so this is undetermined and the UNTRUSTED label is kept. It does not advertise state changes, arbitrary host execution, or sending data to an attacker-chosen destination.

21st_magic_component_inspiration.rationale: The tool `fetch data and previews from 21st.dev` and returns `JSON data of matching components` / `the text snippet for that UI component`. Public component-library data/snippets may be outside-authored and attacker-controllable under the public registry/content threat model. The advertisement does not state whether 21st.dev component data is curated or user-generated, so this is undetermined and the UNTRUSTED label is kept. It does not advertise modifying files itself (`After calling this tool, you must edit or add files`), arbitrary host execution, or delivery to an attacker-chosen destination.

21st_magic_component_refiner.rationale: The tool is for refining a `current UI component`, takes an `Absolute path to the file that needs to be refined`, and `returns redesigned version of the component`. That may require reading and returning contents derived from a local project file, which is non-public host data. The text does not settle whether the tool itself reads the file or only uses context supplied by the agent, so this is undetermined and the SECRET label is kept. It does not advertise arbitrary host execution, attacker-controlled outside content, or delivery to an attacker-chosen destination.

notes: No tool is advertised as off by default.
A fixed vendor/library lookup is not treated as a SINK because no argument selects an attacker-readable destination or arbitrary host.
